question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y$  that satisfies $y(6)=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find the particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y \\ \frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|y| & =\left(x - 6\right)+C\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the exponential function to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|} & ={e}^{\left(x - 6\right)+C} \\ |y| & ={e}^{\left(x - 6\right)+C}\, \\ y & =\pm {e}^{\left(x - 6\right)+C} \\ y & =K{e}^{\left(x - 6\right)}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

where $K=\pm {e}^{C}$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the condition $y(6)=1$ to find $K:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =K{e}^{0} \\ K & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y$ that satisfies the condition $y(6)=1$ is

$$
y={e}^{\left(x - 6\right)}\,.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\left(x + 5\right)}{{y}^{2}}$ that satisfies $y(-3)=\sqrt[3]{13}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2\left(x + 5\right)}{{y}^{2}} \\ {y}^{2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\left(x + 5\right) \\ \int {y}^{2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2\left(x + 5\right)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =\int 2\left(x + 5\right)\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{y}^{3}}{3} & ={\left(x + 5\right)}^{2}+{C}_{1} \\ {y}^{3} & =3{\left(x + 5\right)}^{2}+3{C}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{y}^{3}=3{\left(x + 5\right)}^{2}+C,

We now apply the condition $y(-3)=\sqrt[3]{13}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\sqrt[3]{13})}^{3} & =3(2)^{2}+C \\ 13 & =12+C \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\left(x + 5\right)}{{y}^{2}}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-3)=\sqrt[3]{13}$ is

$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{\left(x - 1\right)}$ that satisfies $y(2)=2.$ Assume that $\left(x - 1\right)>0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find the particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{\left(x - 1\right)} \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)} \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|\left(x - 1\right)|+C \\ \frac{1}{y} & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡|\left(x - 1\right)|+C) \\ y & =-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡|\left(x - 1\right)|+C}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Assuming $\left(x - 1\right)>0,$ the general solution is

$$
y=-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(x - 1\right)+C},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now apply the condition $y(2)=2$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2) & =2 \\ -\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡1+C} & =2 \\ -\frac{1}{C} & =2 \\ C & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{\left(x - 1\right)}$ that satisfies the condition $y(2)=2$ is

$$
y=\frac{-1}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(x - 1\right)-\frac{1}{2})}=\frac{2}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(x - 1\right)}\,.
$$

$$
